title: Concept building from a neutral spec (USG) via the Revit API: staged build, verification and evidence tagging
license_confirmation: I wrote this or have the right to share it, and I agree to publish it under CC BY 4.0 (text/JSON) and MIT (code).

context.tool_or_bridge: RevitBridge MCP (run_csharp, Roslyn 4.8 / C# 12) + desktop screenshots for visual verification

intent: Generate a two-level concept model (levels, slabs, 8 columns, framed glazed facade, flat roof with overhang, terrace railing, two-flight stair, core walls) from a software-neutral JSON building spec plus the source hand sketch, using only native Revit elements, and keep every element traceable to its spec ID and evidence class.
use_when: An agent builds a whole concept model from a structured spec (JSON) through a code-execution bridge
A build script creates many elements of several categories in one call
Element heights depend on a host (roof, slab) that may change later
The model must show which geometry is source fact and which is an AI estimate
not_for: Workshared central models (no sync handling covered here)
Interpreting the sketch itself: that belongs to USG (see IN-0011 redirect)

usage_report.tool_calls: about 25 bridge calls (run_csharp, bridge_status, get_revit_info) plus about 10 desktop screenshots
usage_report.retries: 2 call timeouts (the first write had committed), 4 compile failures from API members that do not exist in Revit 2024, 1 element recreation (wrong slab category), 1 geometry fix found only visually (columns through the roof)
usage_report.without_arpl_estimate: The ARPL index was not consulted before this build. FP05, FP10, FP11, FP13 and FP22 would have prevented or shortened four of the eight problems below.

iterations.instruction: Read-only survey: levels, length units, wall/floor/roof/column/railing/stair types, views. Then showed the user a mapping table (spec item -> evidence class -> Revit element) and the hypotheses before any write.
iterations.result: User corrected the upper-volume placement and glazing module before geometry existed.
iterations.problem: None. Confirms ARPL principle: show the approach before committing.

iterations.instruction: One run_csharp call creating levels, two types, two slabs, 8 columns, 8 curtain walls and 2 core walls.
iterations.result: Bridge returned 'did not respond within 60s'. A read-only follow-up also timed out. bridge_status said the session was alive.
iterations.problem: Revit had committed everything; the call simply outlived the timeout. Re-running would have duplicated all elements.
iterations.found_by: desktop screenshot (no dialog, new level plan in the browser), then a read-only query of elements by Mark

iterations.instruction: Slabs created with type 'Conc 200mm' chosen by name.
iterations.result: Both slabs landed in Structural Foundations.
iterations.problem: The type was a foundation slab (IsFoundationSlab = true). Type change across categories is impossible; slabs were deleted and recreated with a Floors type.
iterations.found_by: category column in the verification query

iterations.instruction: Attach upper walls to the roof with Wall.AddAttachment; build rails with new NonContinuousRailInfo(); commit StairsEditScope without a failures preprocessor.
iterations.result: Compile errors: AddAttachment / AttachmentLocation do not exist in the 2024 API; NonContinuousRailInfo has no public constructor; the bridge helper name was guessed wrong.
iterations.problem: Code written against a remembered API, not the installed one.
iterations.found_by: Roslyn compile errors; fixed by reflecting the types (GetMethods/GetConstructors) and using RailStructure.AddNonContinuousRail and the bridge's Failures() collector

iterations.instruction: Upper columns placed with top constraint = roof-top level (6000).
iterations.problem: Columns pierced the roof: the roof underside at the column positions was lower than the level. When the roof later changed from gable to flat, walls and columns had to be re-derived again.
iterations.found_by: screenshot of a dedicated review 3D view only

iterations.instruction: Curtain wall type with SPACING_LAYOUT_VERT = fixed distance 1500.
iterations.result: Each 10 m face: 6 panels of 1500 plus one 1000 remainder.
iterations.problem: The design intent was '~1.5 m, equal panels'. Switched to maximum spacing 1500: equal panels of 1467 (8.8 m opening) and 1360 (6.8 m opening).
iterations.found_by: panel count in the result + user review

iterations.instruction: Glazing as free-standing full-width curtain walls.
iterations.problem: Design shows a solid frame (corner piers, head band) with recessed glazing. Fixed with a basic wall per face plus a shorter curtain wall on the same line, type with Automatically Embed = Yes; Revit cut the opening itself.
iterations.found_by: user comparing the review view with the sketch

iterations.instruction: Terrace railing from the template's 1100 mm baluster type.
iterations.problem: Design shows three horizontal rails on sparse posts. Duplicated the type, added two non-continuous rails (400, 750) with a 50 x 50 profile, posts at 1500.

iterations.instruction: Promised the user 'one transaction group, one undo' up front, then built in five stages.

final_rule.lesson: 'Committed' is not 'correct' and 'timed out' is not 'failed'. A spec-driven build needs small idempotent stages, semantic type checks, version-checked API calls, host-derived dependent heights and a visual gate after every stage.
final_rule.rule: 1. Stage budget: each write call finishes well inside the bridge timeout (target < 20 s); order: datums + types -> hosts (slabs, walls) -> hosted/dependent (openings, roof, railing, stair). 2. Idempotent writes: find-or-duplicate for types; check for an existing element with the same Mark before creating. 3. Timeout protocol: never retry a write; query state by Mark read-only; if Revit does not answer, take a screenshot before anything else (FP11, FP22). 4. Type semantics: assert category and kind (Floors vs Structural Foundations, basic vs curtain vs stacked wall) before using a type; never choose by name (FP13, FP01). 5. API version gate: reflect the installed API before using non-trivial members (attachments, rails, stairs, failure handling). 6. Dependency re-derivation: record host -> dependant (column top -> roof underside, wall height -> roof underside, opening -> slab) and re-run dependants whenever a host changes (FP10). 7. Visual gate: after each stage, look at a dedicated review 3D view (section box to the building, annotation categories hidden) before reporting success (FP05). 8. Evidence tags: Mark = spec ID, Comments = 'USG | exact / derived / approximate'; promote to 'user-accepted (date)' only on explicit acceptance. 9. Intent-bearing settings (grid layout fixed vs maximum spacing, railing typology, facade composition) are asked or flagged, not defaulted. 10. Undo: one named transaction group per stage; tell the user the real number of undo steps.
final_rule.validation: After each stage: (a) read-only query of all elements whose Comments start with 'USG' returns the expected Marks exactly once each, in the expected categories; (b) for every host-derived element, top elevation <= host underside at its XY; (c) review 3D view screenshot checked against the source sketch before the next stage.

notes: Native elements only were needed: floors, footprint roof, basic + embedded curtain walls, railing, stairs, structural columns. Framed glazing = basic wall + curtain wall with Automatically Embed on the same line. Revit 2024 specifics found: no Wall.AddAttachment; NonContinuousRailInfo is created via RailingType.RailStructure.AddNonContinuousRail(name, height, offset) and then configured (ProfileId); StairsEditScope.Commit needs an IFailuresPreprocessor. Proposed new failure pattern candidate: 'API member assumed from another Revit version' (compile-time face of FP38/FP34?). The spec-side lessons (what the neutral spec failed to carry) are filed separately with USG, not ARPL. No client data: the building is the contributor's own sketch.
